answer: Peers require a scarce ripple bond: each new identity locks spendable POA equal to the median attestation stake of its first five vouchers before any emission. Those vouchers form a kernel cohort that co-signs admission and jointly risk proportional slash if later grading shows the admittee was a sybil. A violet ledger records bond size, cohort edges, and slash history so peers sample high-bond neighbors first and refuse cheap clones that lack bonded vouchers.
